items.headline: Gas prices
items.note: Domestic affordability, export incentives and bargaining power. ACCC gas inquiry provides dated market reports and the LNG netback series. An LNG netback benchmark is not an overseas household bill: comparisons need the same period, market, units, contract basis and treatment of shipping, liquefaction, transport and retail costs. No assertion that overseas consumers always pay less.

items.headline: Corporate tax
items.note: Who contributes and who benefits from resources and data centres. The official 1 October 2026 interview addresses public concerns and the governmentâ€™s response. Company income tax applies to taxable profits, not gross revenue; nil income tax alone does not establish avoidance. Resource royalties, company income tax and petroleum resource rent tax (PRRT) are different measures and must not be conflated. No blanket claim that gas companies pay no tax.

items.headline: Resource profits
items.note: Who receives the value from extraction of publicly owned resources, and how licences, royalties and public-benefit terms should work. Distinct from gas consumer prices, corporate income tax and offshore avoidance. Petroleum ownership is held by Australian governments on behalf of the community; mineral ownership and extraction rights require the relevant jurisdiction and tenure to be identified. Resource ownership and a mining/petroleum licence are not the same thing as surface Crown-land leasehold. Do not assume every extraction project occupies leased Crown land or that all citizens endorse one distribution model. The linked P4A room proposes transparent contracts and public-return tests. The ticker opens the existing Resources Twinkle, an editorial seed with a Public Assets follow-through; its rhetoric is not adopted as a new verified statistical claim.
